beats.beat: Onshore, they read the formulary together, Jory sounding out water-smudged measures matching a fever draught to the stone.
Walter decides to carry the formulary and the stone to a Hartsford healer rather than test it himself, since the measures must be exact and the stone is dangerous to mishandle.
At the healer's door, Walter tries to speak his family name to vouch for the remedy's origin and cannot; he presents the letter itself as proof instead.
Three days later, word returns that the healer's draught, matched to the old measures, has eased the fever moving through Hartsford.

Selah's crew drives the first pilings into the cleared street on schedule, Walter pays Jory in full with a share for Maud's memory, and Jory and Liora start eyeing the fissure itself as their next contract, with Maud agreeing to chart the way first this time.

turn.note: Closes the central mystery and payment while opening the fissure itself as the next job, with Maud's condition (chart first) giving the series its next shape.

listenability: The paragraph beginning 'Three days after that, a girl came down to Floatsome' jumps three days with no break mark, though the sentence does name the new time.
trope_note: Delivers all three: the cursed object's payment resolves exactly as the letter warned, the old-world remedy is proven true in the present, and Maud's insistence on redrawing the chart closes out the mapping-error thread without adding a fourth trope.
fixes: Insert a `break` segment before 'Three days after that, a girl came down to Floatsome with a note for Jory' to mark the time jump cleanly, since the house rule treats a jump without a mark as a fault even when the following sentence names the time.

Open with 'Walter Ames dried his grandmother's formulary' rather than 'the black-bound book,' so a listener who has just heard chapter 7 is anchored by the object's name rather than its description alone.
Consider giving Maud a beat of visible reaction to being paid for her memory beyond 'I'd take it' — a short physical action would land the moment without more dialogue.

findings.quote: They came to the door on Dunnock Lane with an hour of daylight left.
findings.note: The sentence after a scene break has to say when or where we now are — it is the only cue a listener gets that time has passed.
